uuid-generator.intro: Generate unique identifiers for databases, APIs and test data. Choose UUID v4, UUID v1, sortable ULIDs or short Nano IDs, produce up to a thousand at once, and validate existing IDs.
howTo: Pick the identifier type you need.
Set how many to generate and any formatting options.
Press Generate and copy one or all of the results.
Paste an existing ID into the validator to check it.

faqs.a: Yes. UUID v4, ULID and Nano ID all use your browser's crypto.getRandomValues, the same source used for security keys.

faqs.q: What is the difference between UUID v4 and v1?
faqs.a: v4 is entirely random, while v1 embeds a timestamp and is therefore roughly time-ordered but slightly less private.

faqs.q: When should I use a ULID?
faqs.a: When you want a unique ID that also sorts chronologically, which keeps database indexes efficient.
Nano IDs are much shorter than UUIDs while keeping a very low collision risk, making them ideal for URLs and short links.

url-encoder-decoder.name: URL Encoder / Decoder
url-encoder-decoder.description: Free online URL encoder and decoder. Percent-encode query parameters or full URLs, decode escaped text and process many lines at once — privately in your browser.
url-encoder-decoder.intro: Fix broken links and unreadable query strings. Encode text so it can travel safely inside a URL, or decode percent-escaped values back into readable characters, one line at a time or in bulk.
howTo: Choose encode or decode.
Pick component, full URL or Base64URL mode.
Paste your text or URL.
Copy the converted result.

faqs.q: What is the difference between component and full URL encoding?
faqs.a: Component encoding escapes characters such as / ? & = so a value is safe inside a parameter, while full URL encoding leaves the URL structure intact.

faqs.q: When do I need URL encoding?
faqs.a: Whenever a value contains spaces, non-Latin letters or reserved characters such as & and =, which would otherwise break the link.
They are encoded as UTF-8 percent sequences, which every modern browser and server understands.
A Base64 variant that replaces + and / with - and _ so the result is safe inside URLs and JSON Web Tokens.
A stray percent sign or an incomplete escape sequence makes the input invalid, and the tool tells you instead of returning broken text.

html-encoder-decoder.name: HTML Encoder / Decoder
html-encoder-decoder.short: Convert HTML entities to text and back.
html-encoder-decoder.description: Free online HTML entity encoder and decoder. Escape markup, convert named and numeric entities and preview the result safely — all inside your browser.
html-encoder-decoder.intro: Show markup as text or turn entities back into readable characters. Choose how aggressively to escape, and preview the rendered output inside a fully sandboxed frame.
howTo: Choose encode or decode.
Select the encoding depth you need.
Paste your HTML or entity-encoded text.
Copy the result or check the rendered preview.

faqs.a: Escaping prevents user text from being interpreted as markup, which is the basic defence against cross-site scripting.

faqs.q: What do the depth options do?
faqs.a: Basic escapes only the five critical characters, non-ASCII also escapes characters outside ASCII, and all escapes every character as a numeric entity.

faqs.q: Are named entities supported when decoding?
faqs.a: Yes. Named, decimal and hexadecimal entities are all decoded, using the browser's own HTML parser.
Yes. It renders in an iframe with an empty sandbox attribute, so scripts, forms and same-origin access are all disabled.

faqs.q: Does it handle emoji and Arabic text?
faqs.a: Yes, in both directions, including characters made of multiple code points.

json-formatter.name: JSON Formatter & Validator
json-formatter.description: Free online JSON formatter and validator. Beautify or minify JSON, sort keys, explore a tree view and see precise error positions — processed in your browser.
json-formatter.intro: Make sense of unreadable JSON. Format it with the indentation you prefer, validate it with exact error positions, sort keys alphabetically, minify it for production, and explore the structure in a collapsible tree.
howTo: Paste your JSON into the editor.
Press Format to beautify it, or Minify to compact it.
Fix any error using the reported line and column.
Copy the result or browse the tree view.

faqs.q: What are the most common JSON errors?
faqs.a: Trailing commas, single quotes instead of double quotes, unquoted keys and missing brackets. The error message points to the exact line and column.
No. Only whitespace changes, unless you explicitly choose to sort keys.

faqs.q: How large a file can I format?
faqs.a: Several megabytes work comfortably; extremely large files may slow the syntax highlighting.

faqs.q: Is my JSON uploaded for validation?
faqs.a: Never. Parsing and formatting use your browser's own JSON engine.
Yes. Sorting is recursive and makes two versions of the same object much easier to compare.

xml-formatter.name: XML Formatter
xml-formatter.description: Free online XML formatter and validator. Beautify or minify XML, check it is well-formed and convert it to JSON — processed entirely in your browser.
xml-formatter.intro: Turn a single-line XML blob into a readable, indented document. Validate that it is well-formed, count elements and attributes, minify it again for transport, or convert it straight to JSON.
howTo: Paste your XML into the editor.
Press Format to indent it or Minify to compact it.
Check the validation message and the element counts.
Convert to JSON if you need it in another format.

faqs.a: Every tag is closed, elements nest correctly and there is a single root element. It is not the same as being valid against a schema.

faqs.q: Does it validate against a DTD or XSD?
faqs.a: No. It checks that the document is well-formed, which catches the vast majority of practical errors.

faqs.q: How does XML to JSON conversion work?
faqs.a: Elements become objects, repeated elements become arrays and attributes are kept with a prefix so no information is lost.
Comments and CDATA sections survive formatting; JSON conversion keeps text content but drops comments.

faqs.q: Is my XML sent to a server?
faqs.a: No. The browser's built-in DOMParser handles everything locally.

javascript-formatter.intro: Clean up messy or minified JavaScript in one click. Prettier reformats your code with consistent style, Terser compresses it for production, and both run locally so your source never leaves the page.

Press Format to beautify or Minify to compress.
Compare the original and output sizes.
Copy the result or download it as a .js file.

faqs.q: Why does the page take a moment on first use?
faqs.a: The formatter libraries are loaded only when you press the button, which keeps the rest of the site fast.

css-formatter.name: CSS Formatter
css-formatter.description: Free online CSS formatter and minifier. Beautify stylesheets with Prettier or shrink them with our own minifier — processed entirely inside your browser.
css-formatter.intro: Make stylesheets readable again or squeeze them down for production. Formatting uses Prettier, while minification uses our own compact implementation that strips comments and whitespace safely.
howTo: Paste your CSS into the editor.
Press Format for readable output or Minify to compress.
Review the size saving reported below.
Copy the result or download the stylesheet.

faqs.a: Comments, unnecessary whitespace, the final semicolon in a block and redundant zeros, without changing how the styles behave.

faqs.q: Does it work with SCSS or Less?
faqs.a: Plain CSS is fully supported. Preprocessor syntax may format but is not guaranteed to minify correctly.

faqs.q: Are CSS variables and media queries safe?
faqs.a: Yes. Custom properties, media queries, nesting and at-rules are all preserved.

faqs.q: What happens if my CSS has an error?
faqs.a: The tool reports the problem and still returns a best-effort formatted version so you can locate it.
No. Everything runs locally in your browser.

color-converter.description: Free online colour converter. Convert between HEX, RGB, HSL, HSV and CMYK, check WCAG contrast and generate shades — instantly in your browser.

faqs.q: What does the contrast ratio mean?
faqs.a: It compares the brightness of two colours. WCAG asks for at least 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text.

faqs.q: What is the difference between HSL and HSV?
faqs.a: Both describe hue, but HSL is built around lightness while HSV is built around value or brightness, which suits colour pickers.
It is a mathematical approximation. Real print output depends on the colour profile, ink and paper.
